ground_truth: The explanation: Q2 FY2023 had ~$5B of 'pent-up demand' fulfillment from COVID-related supply disruptions on iPhone 14 Pro/Pro Max. Luca noted 'Adjusting for this onetime impact, iPhone revenue would be roughly flat.' Testing against Q3: Q3 FY2024 iPhone was -1% YoY ($39.3B vs $39.7B). Q3 FY2023 did NOT have the same pent-up demand dynamic, yet iPhone still declined slightly. Consistency check: The $5B explanation is specific to Q2's difficult compare. Q3's -1% decline (despite no pent-up demand compare) is consistent with FX headwinds (grew in constant currency per management), competitive pressure in China, and upgrade cycle timing ahead of new iPhone launch. Conclusion: The explanation is internally consistent.
